newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: DRB-Hicom shares seen weaker on requote.
newsitem.headline: DRB-Hicom shares seen weaker on requote.

text.p: Shares of the nine companies linked to the late Malaysian industrialist Yahaya Ahmad are expected to open weaker when they are requoted on Monday, analysts said over the weekend.
The shares were suspended before the opening of trade last Tuesday after Yahaya was killed the night before in a helicopter crash. His wife and the helicopter's pilot were also killed.
Yahaya was chairman of Malaysia's DRB-Hicom group, parent companies of national car maker Proton.

The suspended companies are Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton), vehicle assembler Diversified Resources Bhd (DRB), heavy industrial firm Hicom Holdings Bhd, diversified Gadek (Malaysia) Bhd, timber products concern Golden Pharos Bhd, cement maker Kedah Cement Holdings Bhd, car distributor Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd, financial firm Gadek Capital Bhd, and diversified Eastern Pacific Industrial Corp Bhd.
Analysts said the suspension of the companies had prevented excessive speculation in their shares due to the uncertainty caused by the industrialist's death.
"There have been a lot of sell orders on the stocks from Tuesday," said Sebastian Chang, research manager at Mohaiyani Securities in Kuala Lumpur.

"I had offered Gadek at 19.40 (ringgit) and Proton at 15.90 (ringgit) on Friday, but there were no buyers even at these prices. But I think there are buyers out there" said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
"So I think there will be a sharp sell-off in the morning, then the stocks will come back in the afternoon," he said.
"One rumour is that EPF have allocated two billion ringgit for support of the stocks, but they will probably wait until these come down before they start buying," he added.
The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) is the government's pension fund, and one of the country's largest local institutional investors.
The late Yahaya and his associates -- including newly appointed DRB-Hicom chairman Saleh Sulong -- hold around 65 percent of DRB, the company at the head of the sprawling group.
DRB, Hicom and Gadek would be among the hardest hit, analysts said, with Proton and EON likely to feel less pressure.
Uncertainties over the direction of DRB and Hicom would be the main factors impacting the stocks at the open, said Chang.

DRB and Gadek were also expected to be sold down due to uncertainty over the fate of Yahaya's proportionately larger stakes in these companies. Yahaya and associates hold a direct 32 percent stake in Gadek.
But the future directions of Proton, EON, Kedah Cement and Gadek Capital were assured, said Chang.
"These are one-product companies. Their plans have been outlined, so (there should be) minimum impact," he said.
At the close of trade on Monday (March 3), Proton was at 16 ringgit, DRB at 9.40 and Hicom at 7.10.

DRB and Hicom shares could come down by as much as 10 percent, said Choo Swee Kee, automotive analyst at stockbrokerage Vickers Ballas. He estimated the fall in Proton and EON to be around five percent.
